newsitem.title: UK: Runaway British bishop criticised over story sale.
newsitem.headline: Runaway British bishop criticised over story sale.

text.p: British politicians and churchmen angrily condemned a runaway Roman Catholic bishop who fathered an illegitimate son for selling his story to a Sunday newspaper.
The mass-selling News of the World splashed what it billed as a world exclusive interview with Roderick Wright and the divorced woman with whom he went into hiding nearly two weeks ago.
"I want to apologise for all the hurt and damage we have caused," Wright told the tabloid.
The Wright affair has rocked the Catholic Church in Britain and raised new questions about priestly celibacy.
The News of the World said Wright and divorcee Kathleen MacPhee agreed to speak to the paper for a sum of money that would be paid to her three children.

The tabloid did not give any figure, but parishioners at the former bishop's cathedral at Oban in Scotland gasped at evening mass on Saturday when parish priest Father Sean MacAulay told them: "We have tonight news that our ex-bishop has sold his story to the News of the World for a figure of 300,000 pounds ($465,000) or in that region."
MacAulay told reporters afterwards: "I feel disgusted."

The tabloid's managing editor, Stuart Kuttner, told Britain's Press Association news agency: "The fact is the News of the World has paid a modest five-figure sum for the exclusive story...reports of vast payments in the region of half-a-million are wholly inaccurate."
Home Office Minister Ann Widdecombe, a recent convert to Catholicism, bitterly criticised Wright for selling his story to a newspaper.
"Human frailty is one thing, but deliberate profiteering is quite another," she told the Mail on Sunday.
Cardinal Thomas Winning, head of the Catholic Church in Scotland, said in a statement: "We regard the sale of his story by Roderick Wright as deplorable."
Wright, 56, resigned as bishop three days after going missing with MacPhee from his Scottish diocese.
Another woman later revealed that he was the father of her 15-year-old son.
Church leaders had been appealing to the errant bishop to come forward and answer the allegations.

Wright told the News of the World, which found them at cottage hideaway in England's picturesque northwest Lake District, that he and MacPhee had grown closer as he comforted her while she was seriously ill with cervical cancer.
He said the situation had "developed into something we both recognised as love" but there had been no sexual relationship.
"We have never made love to each other. We have not even shared the same bed or slept together," said Wright. The tabloid quoted him as saying he hoped to wed MacPhee, 41.
Wright said he was sorry for "the neglect and hurt" he had caused his illegitimate son Kevin.
Joanna Whibley, Kevin's mother, told reporters of her astonishment that the bishop had disappeared with MacPhee.
She said Wright had telephoned only a few days before to say that he was finally coming to live with her.
"He is an honest, decent, genuine man and I still love him," Whibley said. "But he compartmentalises things in his head. One day he would be loving, caring and the next day deny his son."

Whibley appealed to Wright on BBC television to come out of hiding. "Roddy, this must stop. You must come out from wherever you are. I know your turmoil and you deserve a real life and forgiveness without limit," she said.
"You are entitled to a number of things and one of those is help from the church. Please make contact with them."
The bishop's brother, Donald Wright, said he was devastated by the revelations and also appealed to Wright to contact him.
Church leaders have been dismayed at the revelations, strenuously denied by Wright three years ago.

Cardinal Winning said Wright had given his superiors "cast-iron guarantees" when confronted with allegations he was having an affair. "We received a categorical denial and a guarantee not only was it untrue but it was scurrilous," said Winning. ($1=.6439 Pound)
